title: Threat model
description: One subject's threat model. The authored artifact is Markdown, because a threat model is written and edited by people; its structure has always been a contract, stated in prose in the skill's schema.md and enforced by regex in the linter. This is that contract as a machine-readable schema, so the model joins every other artifact family instead of being parsed out of prose by three hand-maintained copies of the column list.

subject_id.description: The corpus subject, matching artifact_binding.subject_id. Without it a threat cannot reach its owner.

assets.description: Section 2. One entry per thing worth protecting.

entry_points.description: Section 3. One entry per place untrusted input enters the system or privilege level changes.

threats.description: Section 4. The threat model proper: one row per actor-wants-outcome pair, at the abstraction level where it survives a patch.

deprioritized.description: Section 5. Retired threats. An id here is NEVER reused -- it records that a threat was considered and set aside, which is a different claim from never having considered it.

mitigations.description: Section 8, optional and additive. Each entry is one CLASS-LEVEL control, not a per-finding patch.

attack_scenarios.description: Section 9, optional. The narrative layer for the top 3-5 threats: each scenario tells the attack as it unfolds, in prose.

tenant_boundaries.description: Section 10, optional, MULTI-TENANT SERVICES ONLY. Single-tenant targets omit it; its absence is not a gap. Vocabulary is shared with isolation-review so boundary rows and full reviews line up.

update_history.description: Appended by an update or review pass. Additive: `mode` in provenance keeps its original value.

provenance.description: Section 7. How this model came to exist.

target.description: Path or repo URL at a commit. What was actually modelled.

owner.description: Set for an interview, absent for a bootstrap: a model nobody reviewed must not look reviewed.

harness_version.description: Marks the schema/taxonomy epoch, as metadata.harness_version does for reports. Legacy models predate it.

threat.$comment: A threat is rated with risk_rating (the OWASP Risk Rating Methodology), which every new rating uses, or with the legacy impact/likelihood labels, which stay valid for threats not yet re-rated.

id.description: T1, T2, ... Stable across edits and NEVER renumbered: a removed id is retired, and the next new threat takes the next never-used number. Unique only within this model.

threat.description: One sentence, active voice, naming the outcome. A leading `linddun:` tag marks a row produced by the optional privacy overlay.

actor.description: Weakest-position actor FIRST: scoring reads the first entry.

impact.description: LEGACY label, valid only for threats not yet re-rated; new ratings use risk_rating. Consequence if realised, modelled before reachability is known. Deliberately not the finding severity enum -- `existential` has no severity counterpart.

likelihood.description: LEGACY label, valid only for threats not yet re-rated; new ratings use risk_rating.

status.description: `partially_mitigated` is its own state and the largest bucket in practice; folding it into `mitigated` overstates coverage more than any other collapse here.

evidence.description: Finding or validation identifiers. EMPTY means modelled but not evidenced -- a different claim from unmitigated.

attack_refs.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique ids, validated against the pinned table. Column 11, default for new emissions since harness 0.82.0; this is what an ATT&CK coverage rollup reads.

owasp_llm_references.description: Optional. OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) category IDs for a threat against an LLM, agent or MCP component, the same IDs report findings carry; the category ID is cited, never OWASP text.

atlas_refs.description: Optional. MITRE ATLAS technique or sub-technique IDs (AML.T0051, AML.T0051.000) for a threat against an LLM, agent or MCP component, validated against the pinned ATLAS table like attack_refs.

isolation_dimensions.description: Column 12, optional, multi-tenant only. Which isolation dimension this threat stresses.

review_surfaces.description: Review surfaces this threat sits on, so an audit's threat-model coverage diff maps modelled threats to its review_surface_coverage record.

regulatory_scope.description: Comma-separated regimes governing the asset (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOX, export-control, ...), or `none`.

example_records.description: Concrete field or record names, e.g. `name, email, address` or `kubeconfig, pull-secret`.

trust_boundary.description: The crossing, in free text, e.g. `untrusted file -> process memory`.

reachable_assets.description: Comma-separated names of section-2 assets reachable through this entry point.

review_surfaces.description: Review surfaces reachable through this entry point.

kind.description: What kind of interface this is, so a coverage check can match the entry point to the deterministic pre-scan that enumerates it. Optional: an untagged entry point is reported as unexplained.

review_surfaces.description: Review surfaces (traust-contracts enums/v1/review-surface.json). Optional: an untagged threat, entry point or deprioritized threat is simply not mapped.
Review surfaces the set-aside threat sits on: the model considered the surface and recorded why the threat was not carried. Distinct from no tag, which says nothing about the surface.

id.description: The section-4 threat this scenario narrates.

steps.description: The scenario's prose, one paragraph per entry.

closes_class.description: `no` is worthwhile defence in depth that does not close the class -- recorded rather than dropped.

boundary_id.description: Stable, never renumbered or reused. Aligned with isolation_review.interfaces[].id when a full review exists.

exposure.description: `public` is reachable without tenant credentials; `internal` is control-plane only but carries tenant data.

owasp_risk_rating.description: Risk rating per the OWASP Risk Rating Methodology (OWASP Foundation, https://owasp.org/www-community/OWASP_Risk_Rating_Methodology, CC BY-SA 4.0; reimplemented here in original wording). Every factor is scored 0 to 9. The likelihood score is the mean of its eight factors; the impact score is the mean of the technical or the business factors, per basis. A score below 3 is low, below 6 medium, otherwise high. Severity combines the impact and likelihood levels by the methodology's severity table. Scores, levels and severity are derived values; traust_contracts.v1.risk_rating computes and checks them.

factors.description: Threat-agent factors (skill_level, motive, opportunity, population_size) and vulnerability factors (ease_of_discovery, ease_of_exploit, awareness, intrusion_detection). Higher means more likely.

basis.description: Which factor set sets the impact score. The methodology prefers business impact when it is known, and technical impact otherwise.

severity.description: Overall severity from the impact and likelihood levels.

rationale.description: One short reason per factor, keyed by factor name, so a reviewer can check each score.

canonical_write.description: Opt-in canonical mitigation sizes or null for unknown size; effort remains required.
